newsitem.title: USA: Texas electricity moves higher with tight supply.
newsitem.headline: Texas electricity moves higher with tight supply.

text.p: Spot electricity prices in the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) moved higher Monday as marketers took advantage of some talk of tighter supplies, industry sources said.
Amid the talk, Texas Utilities said its 1,150 megawatt Comanche Peak nuclear unit 2 was expected to hold production at 55 percent of capacity through the week as repairs continued.

On-peak ERCOT power for Tuesday delivery of a 12-16 hour block was talked in the $20.50-21.50 range from weekend power discussion in a range of $19.00-20.00 per megawatt hour (MWh), the brokers and marketers said.
Off-peak next-day power was pegged in the $13.50-14.50 range from $12.00-13.50 over the weekend, the sources said.
Off-peak electricity for the remainder of September was discussed near $13.50, the sources said.
October on-peak ERCOT power was said to have moved up to the $18.25-18.75 range with one unconfirmed trade said to have been done at $18.25 per MWh, the brokers and marketers said.
October power was discussed in the $17.75-18.10 range late last week.
-- Chris Reese, New York Power Desk 212-859-1627
